notes.1: Just over half of all candidates correctly identified B as the correct answer. Over 35% of more able candidates and over 25% of less able candidates selected D. D cannot be correct, since with a two dimensional image of the leaf, it is not possible to know what the surface area or volume is. Just under half of all candidates included the presence of epithelium in their answers. Epithelium is only found in animals. �PAGE�12
notes.2: The relative difficulty of this question was due to many candidates not understanding the processes involved in transpiration. It is the evaporation of water from mesophyll cell walls that determines rate of water movement from roots to leaves.
notes.3: The majority of more able candidates and almost half the less able candidates correctly identified the structure of mature xylem vessel elements and a phloem sieve tube element.
notes.4: The majority of candidates were able to identify the apoplastic pathway.
notes.5: This was answered correctly by nearly 90% of all candidates.
notes.6: This was answered correctly by nearly 90% of all candidates. However, over 10% of less able candidates did not realise that the atrio-ventricular valves open and close together.
notes.7: Almost 40% of the less able candidates did not know the difference between a closed or open circulatory system and 35% of them did not know the features of a single or double circulatory system.
notes.8: Almost half of the less able candidates did not know the properties of components of the cell surface membrane.
notes.9: Nearly 70% of less able candidates and 25% of more able candidates did not appreciate that if water enters the stalk, from high to low water potential, the thin walled inner cells would bend more easily than the thick walled outer cells.
notes.10: Less able candidates continue to find it difficult to relate water potentials to different solute concentrations.
notes.11: Whilst over 90% of candidates knew that an active site was found on sucrase, over 20% of less able candidates confused hydrolysis and condensation.
notes.12: Almost 20% of less able candidates continue to have difficulty in learning the food tests. Questions 13–15 Biochemistry continues to be well understood by more able candidates, whilst the majority of the less able candidates did not know the correct answer.
notes.16: The features of triglycerides were understood by almost all of the more able candidates and 50% of the less able candidates. �PAGE�13
notes.17: Only 40% of all candidates were able to identify the different types of white blood cell. Candidates should have looked at prepared slides of blood smears.
notes.18: Less able candidates continue to have difficulty with the differences between antibody and antigen and the roles of T helper cells and B-lymphocytes.
notes.19: This was well answered by the more able candidates. Over half of the less able candidates could not identify the diseases caused by bacteria.
notes.20: Half of all candidates realised that all three reasons could cause an outbreak of malaria in a country where it had been eliminated.
notes.21: More able candidates understood the concepts of immunity very well.
notes.22: A significant number of candidates incorrectly thought that endoplasmic reticulum was visible under high power of a light microscope. Candidates who had observed slides of plant cells were aware that the only organelles clearly visible would be chloroplasts.
notes.23: Almost 60% of all candidates realised that the purpose of calibrating the graticule is to use it to make measurements.
notes.24: It was encouraging that over 70% of candidates gave the correct answer.
notes.25: Over 80% of all candidates know the characteristics of a prokaryotic cell.
notes.26: Whilst the more able candidates were able to identify the correct rows, many less able candidates incorrectly thought that mitochondria have no enzymes or that transcription occurs in the rough endoplasmic reticulum.
notes.27: Less able candidates do not fully appreciate the dynamics of enzyme-catalysed reactions.
notes.28: 40% of less able candidates realised that all three factors might regulate an enzyme-catalysed reaction.
notes.29: Whilst this question presented a lot of information, the more able candidates could successfully process it to obtain the correct answer. �PAGE�14
notes.30: Only just over 30% of candidates did not realise that male bees could not be genetically identical.
notes.31: It was pleasing that over 80% of all candidates understood the process of semi-conservative replication in DNA.
notes.32: Nearly 90% of all candidates answered this question correctly.
notes.33: This was poorly answered by 35% of less able candidates. Knowledge of the structure of DNA is a fundamental requirement of modern biology courses.
notes.34: More able candidates generally had little difficulty in processing this information. Since uracil replaces thymine in RNA, column C must be thymine. With adenine and thymine pairing up in DNA, column B must represent adenine.
notes.35: The majority of candidates correctly answered this question.
notes.36: A significant number of less able candidates do not know the structure of alveoli and trachea.
notes.37: It was pleasing that 75% of candidates understood the role of nicotine in increasing the risk of cardiovascular disease.
notes.38: The percentage transfer between the Sun and producers was 1%, between the producers and primary consumers is 10%, between the primary consumers and secondary consumers is 20% and between detritus and decomposers is 80%.
notes.39: Almost half of all candidates were able to process this information to realise that the only microorganisms that would not increase would be denitrifying bacteria which require anaerobic conditions.
notes.40: Candidates found it difficult to use the data in the table to calculate the energy values for each species. All that was required was to multiply the number of individuals by the biomass and multiply this by the energy value. S has a value of 450 000, P a value of 1000, Q a value of 100 and R a value of 1.8. �PAGE�15
